name: scpi-fake
experiment:
# Oscilloscope waveform capture through the SCPI plugin.
#
# The default run uses the plugin's in-process SYNTHETIC oscilloscope, so it
# needs no instrument. Its 1 kHz sine is generated, not measured:
#
#   HWLAB_SCPI_FAKE=rigol hwlab run --yes examples/scpi-fake.yaml     # or siglent
#
# For a real instrument (UNVALIDATED: the Rigol and Siglent command sets were
# written from public documentation and never run against hardware):
#
#   export HWLAB_SCPI_HOSTS="scope=tcp://192.168.1.50"     # or serial:/dev/ttyUSB0@115200
#   hwlab devices                                           # scpi/scope
#   hwlab invoke scpi/scope SCPI.identify
#
# and replace `device:` with scope. A capture is acquire-and-export, like
# Saleae: it never streams. `trigger: single` arms the instrument and waits for
# a real trigger; `none` reads whatever the instrument currently holds.
name: scpi-fake
duration: 4s

devices:
  scope:
    plugin: scpi
    device: fake-rigol
    channels: [1, 2]
    trigger: single
    trigger_timeout_s: 5
    screenshot: true

steps:
  - {name: identify, at: 100ms, device: scope, call: SCPI.identify}
  - {name: vpp,      at: 200ms, device: scope, call: Oscilloscope.measure, args: {item: vpp, channel: 1}}

plots:
  - name: scope
    title: Synthetic oscilloscope capture
    format: svg

clock.source: host clock (synthetic instrument: no real acquisition)
clock.note: SYNTHETIC oscilloscope; times only order the events
